title: Intermediate varieties are numerically rarer than the forms they connect

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intermediate varieties are numerically rarer than the forms they connect

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Where varieties intermediate between two other forms occur in nature, they are generally much rarer numerically than the forms they connect, because they inhabit narrower intermediate zones.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: generally when varieties intermediate between two other forms occur, they are much rarer numerically than the forms which they connect.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Absence or rarity of transitional varieties.”. Scope: varieties of plants and animals in nature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The abundance comparison is clear for documented clines and hybrid zones. A general assessment requires compiling scattered genotype and census data beyond what current integrated databases provide.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify phenotypically or genetically intermediate natural populations and compare their abundance or occupancy with the two endpoint forms under standardized sampling. Lower abundance of intermediates across systems supports the claim; equal or greater abundance refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Intermediate varieties are inconsistently named and sampled.

Narrow range alone can create low total abundance without lower local fitness.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Numerical rarity of intermediate forms can be proxied by abundance and area in hybrid zones, especially in birds. The varieties in the wording are not a stable modern category, and non-bird data are mostly presence-only. Under-description of intermediates biases the test toward finding them rare, which limits how strongly a positive result would count.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify phenotypically intermediate populations between two forms and compare their abundance or occupied area with the forms they connect. Much smaller counts for the intermediates would confirm the claim; intermediates as numerous as the endpoint forms would refute it. Subspecies and hybrid-zone censuses are the operational stand-in for varieties.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hybrid zones can be dense locally even when the intermediate phenotype is geographically narrow.

Intermediate varieties are under-described, so the rarest ones are missing.

Occurrence density is a poor abundance measure outside well-watched birds.
